⁶ Then he summoned his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel. ⁷ David said to Solomon, "My son, I had it in my heart to build a house for the name of the LORD my God. ⁸ But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 'You have shed much blood and waged great wars. You shall not build a house for my name, because you have shed so much blood on the earth before me. ⁹ Listen — a son will be born to you, a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side; his name will be Solomon, and I will grant Israel peace and quiet during his reign. ¹⁰ He is the one who will build a house for my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'"

¹¹ "Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, so that you may succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, as he has promised concerning you. ¹² Only may the LORD give you wisdom and understanding, and commission you over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God. ¹³ You will succeed if you are careful to follow the statutes and ordinances that the LORD gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous — do not be afraid or discouraged. ¹⁴ Now, with great effort I have provided for the house of the LORD a hundred thousand talents of gold, a million talents of silver, and quantities of bronze and iron too great to weigh, along with timber and stone. You may add to them. ¹⁵ You have plenty of craftsmen — stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and every kind of skilled worker.

¹⁶ Gold and silver, bronze and iron — it is all beyond counting. Get up and get to work, and may the LORD be with you." ¹⁷ David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son: ¹⁸ "Is not the LORD your God with you? Has he not given you rest on every side? He has handed the inhabitants of this land over to me, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before his people. ¹⁹ Now devote your heart and soul to seeking the LORD your God. Rise up and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God into the house that will be built in honor of the LORD's name."

⁶ David divided them into groups according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. ⁷ The sons of Gershon were Laadan and Shimei. ⁸ The sons of Laadan: Jehiel the chief, then Zetham and Joel — three in all. ⁹ The sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran — three. ¹¹ Jahath was the chief and Zizah was second. ⁶ Shemaiah son of Nethaneel, a Levite scribe, recorded the assignments before the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the priestly and Levite families — one family being drawn for Eleazar and then one for Ithamar. ⁷ The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah, ⁸ the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim, ⁹ the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin, ¹⁰ the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,

¹¹ the ninth to Jeshuah, the tenth to Shecaniah, ¹² the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim, ¹³ the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab, ¹⁴ the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer, ¹⁵ the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Aphses,

²¹ Concerning Rehabiah: from his sons, Isshiah was the chief. ²² Of the Izharites: Shelomoth, and from his sons came Jahath. ²³ The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth. ²⁴ Of the sons of Uzziel: Michah; and from Michah's sons came Shamir. ²⁵ Michah's brother was Isshiah, and from Isshiah's sons came Zechariah.

[Chapter 28] ¹ David assembled all the leaders of Israel in Jerusalem — the tribal commanders, the commanders of the divisions that served the king, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the officials over all the king's property and livestock, the palace officials, the soldiers and warriors, every man of standing. ² King David rose to his feet and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had my heart set on building a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD — a footstool for our God — and I made preparations for building it. ³ But God said to me, 'You shall not build a house for my name, because you have been a warrior and have shed blood.' ⁴ Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from my whole family to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah as the leading tribe, and from Judah he chose my father's family, and from among my father's sons he was pleased to make me king over all Israel. ⁵ Of all my sons — for the LORD has given me many — he has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.

⁶ "He said to me, 'Your son Solomon will build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father. ⁷ I will establish his kingdom forever, if he holds firmly to carrying out my commands and ordinances, as he does now.' ⁸ So in the sight of all Israel, the LORD's assembly, and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek out all the commands of the LORD your God, so that you may hold this good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your descendants forever. ⁹ And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father and serve him with wholehearted devotion and a willing spirit, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every intention behind every thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you abandon him, he will reject you forever. ¹⁰ Consider carefully now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house as the sanctuary. Be strong and do the work."

[Chapter 29] ¹ Then King David said to the whole assembly, "My son Solomon — the one whom God has chosen — is young and inexperienced, and the work is enormous, for this palace is not being built for a human being but for the LORD God. ² With all my resources I have provided for the temple of my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, wood for the wood, onyx for the settings, turquoise, stones of various colors, all kinds of fine stone, and marble — great quantities of it. ³ Besides all this, in my devotion to the temple of my God I give from my personal treasury of gold and silver — over and above everything I have already provided — ⁴ three thousand talents of gold from Ophir and seven thousand talents of refined silver for overlaying the walls of the buildings; ⁵ gold for the gold work and silver for the silver — everything that will be made by craftsmen. Now, who is willing to consecrate himself today to the LORD?"

⁶ Then the family heads and officers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king's work gave willingly. ⁷ They donated toward the work on God's temple: five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron. ⁸ Those who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite. ⁹ The people rejoiced because these offerings were given freely and wholeheartedly. King David also rejoiced greatly. ¹⁰ David praised the LORD in the presence of the whole assembly, saying, "Praise be to you, LORD, the God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

¹¹ "Yours, LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the splendor and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth is yours. In your hands are strength and power to exalt and give strength to all. ¹³ Now, our God, we give you thanks and praise your glorious name. ¹⁴ But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from your hand. ¹⁵ We are foreigners and strangers in your sight, as were all our ancestors. ¹⁶ "LORD our God, all this abundance that we have provided for building you a temple for your holy name comes from your hand, and it all belongs to you. ¹⁷ I know, my God, that you test the heart and are pleased with integrity. And the whole assembly praised the LORD, the God of their fathers, bowing low and prostrating themselves before the LORD and the king.
